title: Validation of Quality-of-Life Questionnaires in Chronic Eye Diseases
summary:
People with chronic uveitis often experience limitations in visual function and quality of life. To better capture these burdens, questionnaires are used. The standard questionnaire (VFQ-25), however, is relatively long. Therefore, it will be evaluated whether a shorter version (VFQ-9) is similarly reliable and more suitable for regular use.
The study investigates whether the short questionnaire measures quality of life as effectively as the long version, whether it performs well across all uveitis subtypes, and whether it is reliably completed by patients, both in the clinic and at home.
A total of 150 adults with various forms of uveitis complete both the long and short questionnaires during a clinic visit. One week later, they complete both questionnaires again online. The responses are then compared to assess the accuracy, reliability, and completion rate of the short questionnaire.

interventions.name: Patients with uveitis are asked to complete the VFQ-25 and VFQ-9 quality-of-life questionnaires twice, one week apart. The first assessment takes place on site, and the second is conducted online.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Non-infectious anterior, intermediate, posterior uveitis, or panuveitis as the primary diagnosis
-Good German language skills (able to communicate confidently with medical staff about personal symptoms and disease course; assessed at the discretion of the study personnel)
Exclusion criteria:
-Primary glaucoma and other chronic eye diseases that affect quality of life
-Active uveitis (defined as >1+ anterior chamber cells, new vitreous cells, or new uveitis findings on the retina or optic disc)
